coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia "2024 Ohio State Buckeyes football team", fetched as SECTION-SCOPED RAW WIKITEXT: https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football_team&action=raw&section=34 (the "Roster" section, which carries the roster-footer coaching staff list) and &section=4 (the "Additions" table). IMPORTANT FOR THE VERIFIER: fetching the ordinary article URL (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football_team) does NOT work for these quotes — I tested it and the fetcher truncates the page well before the roster footer, so none of the 27 staff-list lines appear. The section-scoped raw URLs above were tested and return the quoted lines verbatim. (2) The school's own staff directory archived on the Wayback Machine at https://web.archive.org/web/20250110082527/https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/sports/football/roster — a snapshot from January 10, 2025, ten days before the January 20, 2025 CFP National Championship win over Notre Dame. This is the best possible "at the championship game" evidence and it yielded 62 directory entries (61 unique people; Parker Wereb is listed twice under two duplicate records).

MAJOR CAVEAT ON THE WAYBACK QUOTES — PLEASE READ. ohiostatebuckeyes.com is a client-side-rendered Sidearm/Next.js app. The staff directory is NOT in the page's visible HTML text; it lives in an embedded JSON payload inside a <script> block. I confirmed the archived page renders only ~6,500 characters of visible text and contains none of the staff names as prose. Therefore every Wayback quote I supply is the exact byte-level JSON substring (e.g. "title":"General Manager, Player Personnel","firstName":"Mark ","lastName":"Pantoni"), copied verbatim from the raw HTML, including the site's / escaping for slashes and its stray trailing spaces in some name fields. These will string-match ONLY if the verifier fetches raw HTML. If the verifier converts to markdown or strips scripts, EVERY Wayback quote will fail. Additionally, WebFetch in my environment could not reach web.archive.org at all (it errored outright); I retrieved these snapshots via direct curl. If the verifier's fetcher shares that limitation, all Wayback citations will be unretrievable regardless of quoting. For the 27 people who appear in both sources I listed Wikipedia first precisely so they survive that scenario; the 34 support-staff-only rows have no fallback and would all drop.

ROLE WORDING. For people in both sources I set `role` to the school's own wording from the January 2025 directory (the more authoritative and more granular phrasing), with the Wikipedia line as the second source using its own slightly different wording (e.g. school says "Quality Control (Offense)" where Wikipedia says "Quality control - offense"). Both quotes are verbatim to their respective sources.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT / KNOWN GAPS. (a) I could not obtain the 2024 media guide. No media-guide PDF surfaced on ohiostatebuckeyes.com, archive.org or issuu within my reach, so there is no third independent staff list here. (b) My WebSearch budget was exhausted at the very start of this task (200/200 calls already consumed before I began), so I could NOT run contemporary news searches for hire announcements, mid-season staff changes, or support-staff coverage. Everything here comes from the two sources above plus citations already embedded in the Wikipedia article. This is the single biggest limitation on completeness — there may be additional analysts, interns, or student assistants documented only in news coverage that I had no ability to search for. (c) I verified staff continuity only at two points (an August 23, 2024 snapshot and the January 10, 2025 snapshot). Comparing them, the directory was stable across the season with three changes: Josh Miller ("Program Assistant") appears in August but NOT in January and is therefore excluded from this list; Nairan Normand and Morgan Phillips appear in January but not August. I could not pin down exact arrival/departure dates for those three, so I have flagged Normand and Phillips with midseason_note rather than guessing. (d) I did NOT verify anyone's presence at the championship game itself beyond the January 10 directory; a departure in the final ten days would be invisible to me. (e) The athletics site's football directory mixes football-specific staff with shared athletic-department personnel (compliance, creative media, athletic training). I included them because the task asks for everyone documented on the team's staff, but a ring-counting rule may want to treat, say, the Associate AD for Compliance differently from a position coach. I have categorized them honestly rather than inflating the on-field count.

EXCLUSIONS (deliberate, not oversights). Brandon Jordan was hired February 2024 as "Program assistant - defense" but Wikipedia footnotes that he "left the program after three months" — he was gone before the season and appears in neither directory snapshot, so I excluded him. I also excluded the seven documented offseason DEPARTURES who were not on staff during 2024 (Tony Alford, Mike Dawson, Corey Dennis, Perry Eliano, Todd Fitch, Parker Fleming, Joe Philbin). Parker Wereb is listed once despite two duplicate directory records. Nothing in this list is inferred, reconstructed from memory, or padded — every one of the 61 rows comes from a directory entry or wikitext line I actually retrieved.
